items.subject: Petition under Section 79(1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003, read with Regulation 17 and 18 of the CERC (Terms and Conditions for Renewable Energy Certificates for Renewable Energy Generation) Regulations, 2022, seeking condonation of delay in complying with the procedure of issuance of Renewable Energy Certificates for FY 2023-24 and other consequential reliefs. Petition under Section 79(1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003, read with Regulation 17 and 18 of the CERC (Terms and Conditions for Renewable Energy Certificates for Renewable Energy Generation) Regulations, 2022, seeking condonation of delay in complying with the procedure of issuance of Renewable Energy Certificates for FY 2023-24 and other consequential reliefs.

3. The Petitioner has filed the present petition under Section 79(1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 17 and 18 of the CERC (Terms and Conditions for Renewable Energy Certificates for Renewable Energy Generation) Regulations, 2022 (REC Regulations, 2022) for seeking condonation of delay in complying with the procedure of issuance of Renewable Energy Certificates (REC) for FY 2023-24 and other consequential reliefs.

- (b) _Direct NLDC to issue Renewable Energy Certificates for FY 2023-24 in favour of the Petitioner;_

- (c) _Pass any other or further order(s) as this Hon’ble Commission may deem fit and proper in the interest of justice._

- (b) The Petitioner was unable to approach the NLDC for issuance of RECs within the period of three months from the end of the financial year as stipulated under Regulation 10(3) of the REC Regulations 2022. Due to various reasons beyond the control of the Petitioner, substantial time was consumed in completing the aforesaid steps, as elaborated below:

- (d) The Petitioner complied with all requirements under the REC Regulations 2022 and obtained all approvals and recommendations certifying its eligibility and entitlement to the RECS for FY 2023-24.

- (e) Therefore, the Petitioner requests the Commission to exercise its power to relax under Regulation 18 of the REC Regulations, 2022, to (i) condone the delay of eight-two (82) days in approaching NLDC; and (ii) direct NLDC to issue RECs in favour of the Petitioner for FY 2023-24.

2. During the course of the hearing, no one was present on behalf of the Petitioner. However, considering the nature of the dispute involved in the Petition, the Commission admitted the Petition and issued notice to the Respondent. The Commission also directed the Respondent to file its reply and the Petitioner to file its rejoinder, if any.

3. During the course of the hearing, the counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the present Petition was filed seeking condonation of the delay of 82 days in approaching the NLDC for issuance of RECs for FY 2023-24, in terms of the REC Regulations, 2022. The counsel for the Petitioner also submitted that under Regulation 10(3), the application for issuance of RECs was required to be filed within three months of the end of the financial

year; however, due to reasons beyond the Petitioner's control, the prescribed timeline could not be adhered to. It was also submitted that the Commission condoned similar delay in its several orders. The Counsel further pointed out that despite the lapse of considerable time, the Respondent, NLDC, did not file any reply in the matter. Considering the submissions of the counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission granted another opportunity to the Respondent to file its reply, if any and the Petitioner, to file its rejoinder.

4. Due to a paucity of time, the matter could not be taken for the hearing and was accordingly adjourned.

5. During the course of the hearing, the counsel of the Respondent, NLDC, submitted that the Respondent did not wish to file any reply in the matter, and the Commission may consider the prayers of the Petitioner as may be deemed fit. Further, on the request of the counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission permitted the Petitioner to file its note of submissions. Subject to the above, the Commission reserved the matter for order.

6. Accordingly, on 14.02.2026, the Petitioner submitted the short note of the submissions.

7. The Commission has heard the learned counsels for the Petitioner and the Respondent and has carefully perused the records.

10. From the above, we observe that the Petitioner was required to approach the Respondent, NLDC, within three months from the end of the financial year, along with the received certification from APERC. We observe that the Petitioner could not adhere to the timeline and has applied for issuance of RECs for FY 2023-24 with a delay of 82 days. As submitted by the Petitioner, the delay was due to various factors, primarily related to the collection and collation of renewable energy procurement data and compliance with the requisite regulatory and procedural requirements. Further, during the hearing, the Respondent, NLDC, submitted that the Commission may consider the Petitioner's prayers as it deems fit.

_The Commission may, from time to time, issue such practice directions and orders as considered appropriate for the implementation of these regulations_

_The Commission may by general or special order, for reasons to be recorded in writing, and after giving an opportunity of hearing to the parties likely to be affected, may relax any of the provisions of these regulations on its own motion or on an application made before it by interested person(s)._

13. In our view, the delay in the application for issuance of the REC is procedural in nature due to the reasons stated by the Petitioner and is not likely to prejudice any of the stakeholders, including the Respondent. Accordingly, the timelines stipulated under Regulation 10(3) of the REC Regulations 2022 are hereby relaxed, and the Petitioner is permitted to file its application for the issuance of RECs before the Central Agency for FY 2023-24.

14. Further, the Respondent NLDC is directed to issue the RECs for FY 2023-24 to the Petitioner, APCPDCL, after due verification and satisfying itself that the Petitioner meets all other conditions and has submitted all the required documents for the issuance of RECs.

items.subject: Petition seeking permission to continue interchange of infirm power including drawl of Start-Up Power from the grid as per CERC Deviation Settlement Mechanism (DSM) Regulation 2024 read with Regulation 19 of Indian Electricity Grid Code (IEGC) beyond 30/06/2026 till the COD of RAPP-8 or 30/06/2027, whichever is earlier & anticipated delay in commissioning of Unit#8 of the 2x700MWe Rajasthan Atomic Power Project-7&8 (RAPP-8), Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL), Mumbai 400094. Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited
items.pdf_digest:
Petition seeking permission to continue interchange of infirm power including drawl of Start-Up Power from the grid as per CERC Deviation Settlement Mechanism (DSM) Regulation 2024 read with Regulation 19 of Indian Electricity Grid Code (IEGC)   beyond 30/06/2026 till the COD of RAPP-8 or 30/06/2027, whichever is earlier & anticipated delay in commissioning of Unit#8 of the 2x700MWe Rajasthan Atomic Power Project7&8 (RAPP-8), Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL), Mumbai 400094.

Shri Naman Saraswat, Advocate, NPCIL Ms. Jyoti Thakur, NPCIL Shri Rahul Bisht, NPCIL

This Petition has been filed by the Petitioner, Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited, under Regulation 19 of Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Indian Electricity Grid Code) Regulations, 2023 (hereinafter referred to as ‘the Grid Code’) as amended from time to time, with the following prayers:

- _(a) To permit drawl of start-up power from the grid under Deviation Settlement Mechanism (DSM) for RAPP-8 commissioning till COD of RAPP-8 or 30/06/2027, whichever is earlier._

- (a) The Rajasthan Atomic Power Project-7&8 (RAPP-7&8) comprises two units of 700 MWe each, based on indigenous Pressurized Heavy Water Reactor (PHWR) technology, situated at Rawatbhata, District Chittorgarh, Rajasthan. RAPP-7, the first unit of the twin-unit module, commenced Commercial Operation on 15.04.2025. RAPP-8, the second unit, is an indigenous 700 MWe PHWR and has been drawing start-up power under the Deviation Settlement Mechanism (DSM) since 17.03.2024, pursuant to Start-Up Transformer (SUT-8A & 8B) charging in March 2024. The permission for drawal of start-up power from the grid for RAPP-8 was granted vide Order dated 18.06.2025 in Petition No. 630/MP/2025, which permitted such drawal till the first synchronization of RAPP-8 or 30.6.2026, whichever is earlier. As the first synchronization of RAPP-8 could not be achieved by 30.6.2026, the Petitioner has filed the present petition seeking further extension of the permission for drawal of start-up power beyond 30.6.2026 till the COD of RAPP-8 or 30.6.2027, whichever is earlier.

- (c) Regarding the current status of commissioning activities, the Petitioner has submitted as follows:

**3.** The matter was admitted on 02.06.2026, and notices were issued to the Respondent. The Petitioner submitted that the present Petition has been filed seeking permission to continue interchange of infirm power, including drawal of Start-up Power from the grid as per the Deviation Settlement Mechanism Regulations 2024, read with Regulation 19 of the Indian Electricity Grid Code 2023, beyond 30.6.2026 till the COD of RAPP-8 or 30.6.2027, whichever is earlier. The learned counsel highlighted that RAPP-8 is a first-of-a-kind indigenous 700 MWe PHWR and that the stringent Quality Assurance requirements for critical equipment, combined with the limited availability of qualified vendors in India, have contributed to the delays in project execution. The learned counsel further submitted that the Respondent/NRLDC had not filed any reply despite notice, and requested that the matter be reserved for orders. Accordingly, the Commission reserved the matter for order.

4. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner. Regulation 13 of the CERC (Grant of Connectivity, Long-term Access and Medium-term Open Access in

inter-State Transmission and related matters) Regulations, 2009 (as amended) ('GNA Regulations') provides as under:

_Provided that the concerned Regional Load Despatch Centre while granting such permission shall keep grid security in view._

_(2) The period for which such inter-change shall be allowed shall be as follows:_

_(b) Injection of infirm power shall not exceed one year from the date of first synchronization._

6. A reading of the aforesaid provisions makes it clear that under Regulation 19(1) of the Grid Code, a unit of a generating station that has been granted connectivity to the inter-State Transmission System in accordance with GNA Regulations is allowed to interchange power with the grid during the commissioning period, including testing and full load testing before the COD, after obtaining the prior permission of the concerned RLDC. Further, under Regulation 19(3), this Commission has the jurisdiction and power to allow an extension of the period for interchange of power beyond the stipulated period, upon an application made by the generating station at least two months in advance  of the stipulated period’s completion. The present petition has been filed in advance of the expiry of the permission granted vide Order dated 18.06.2025 in Petition No. 630/MP/2025, and is, therefore, within the stipulated period prescribed under Regulation 19(3) of the Grid Code.

8. The Commission has considered the submissions and the circumstances stated by the Petitioner as set out in paragraph 7 above. In the given facts and circumstances, we are inclined to invoke our power under Regulation 19(3) of the Grid Code. We are of the view that the non-availability of start-up power would hamper the progress of the remaining commissioning activities and result in further delay in achieving criticality,

synchronization, and commercial operation of RAPP-8. Accordingly, in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case, and as an exceptional measure, we hereby allow the extension of time for the drawal of start-up power from the grid under the Deviation Settlement Mechanism (DSM), as sought, till the Commercial Operation Date (COD) of RAPP-8 or 30.6.2027, whichever is earlier. The Commission expects the Petitioner to make every effort to ensure the earliest possible commercial operation of RAPP-8.
